entities.name: Jewish Museum
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Jewish Museum Berlin, designed by architect Daniel Libeskind and opened in 2001, is the most architecturally and emotionally radical museum building of the 20th century — a titanium-zinc zinc-clad structure of intersecting and fragmented lines that deliberately disorients visitors, uses slanted floors, narrow windows (called 'voids'), and dead-end corridors (the Holocaust Tower, the Garden of Exile) to simulate the disorientation, isolation, and despair experienced by Jews in Nazi Germany. The building is considered the masterwork of deconstructivist architecture.

Libeskind won the 1989 competition with a design titled 'Between the Lines' — two intersecting lines, one straight (German-Jewish history in continuity) and one zigzag (the broken, fragmented history of Jewish suffering). The building's plan is a distorted Star of David; windows are cut at angles derived from addresses of Berlin Jews who were murdered; the six pointed voids that cut through all floors represent the void left by destroyed Jewish life. The Holocaust Tower — a dark, bare concrete chamber lit only by a thin slit of light far above — is entered and then sealed, creating profound claustrophobia.

The permanent collection documents 2,000 years of German-Jewish history — from the Ashkenazi cultural formation to the Holocaust and its aftermath. The museum reopened in 2020 after a major renovation. The Jewish Museum Berlin's building became so famous as architecture that the institution was forced to open the building to visitors before any collection was installed — people came to experience the architecture itself. Libeskind's design influenced Holocaust memorial architecture globally.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Jewish Museum Berlin — through Libeskind's radical deconstructivist architecture that physically simulates persecution's disorientation — proved that a building's form could carry moral meaning as powerfully as its collection, transforming museum architecture globally.
